searchText: Wonder, what are the reasons we put state.balances separate from state.validators? Is it so that certain operations are cheaper? What are those operations? General idea is to segregate a high-frequency changing thing from a lower frequency changing thing. By doing this we can save on recomputation during the tree hash If balance was a field of validator, then you would have to re-hash a lot more data for every state root By separating the balances out, you can cache large parts of the beacon state hash tree root computation https://notes.ethereum.org/jDcuUp3-T8CeFTv0YpAsHw?view mentions briefly it is to reduce rehashing as well So, the new nested structure for tests is nearly complete (completed test gen updating, working on documentation). This includes updating the SSZ-static tests (handler = ssz type, suite = randomization mode, case = variation with RNG seed), this cover all phase 0 types (or at least the valid-encoding case). But I am not sure how to go about the old SSZ-generic tests. We don't really have a way to describe a type between different languages, and the old integer tests are not that great. Does anyone have some ideas how to go about extending/changing ssz-generic? One of the options on the table is porting over the set of SSZ tests the pyspec uses, https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/blob/dev/test_libs/pyspec/eth2spec/utils/ssz/test_ssz_impl.py And then make the types used in that test part of the format spec, since we cannot describe the type dynamically. The SSZ specs already define the SSZ types in a language agnostic way though Not in a way that the type can be parsed from a test file We don't have something like the ABI encoding for SSZ (afaik), just python-esque spec description mmmh, we could have {"kind": "Vector", "data": [{"kind": "uint64", "value": 123}, {"kind": "uint64", "value": 456}]}, but that's very noisy and error prone, don't want mixed types in a vector or list are there still heterogeneous containers? Well, container can have mixed fields. But lists/vectors don't have mixed type elements. The old ssz-generic generator has a type definition renderer, but it's super outdated so a field could be ``` - field - container: List / Vector / Literal - element: uint64 - value: [1, 2, 3] / 123 ``` Thanks for the input, but it's not trivial. It needs to parse somehow, and nest elegantly somehow. Yeah I know, and it complicates the test suite especially for static languages I think folder-based types and client hardcode the type deserialization might be simpler, unless we expect lots of new mixed/nested test in the future It's tempting to just remove the ssz-generic. Clients are welcome to copy over the cases of `test_ssz_impl.py`, and can do so in their own language/test agnostic way. On the other end, fuzzing would be more effective if we can make the fuzzer do any random type, instead of just the phase 0 types. The main value of SSZ generics is for client to test and agree on exceptional or invalid serialization/deserialization ssz-static is already doing randomization. Just not the invalid cases (e.g. invalid offsets). The fuzzer could do that technically, but the types are still a problem We can choose to focus it on just the base types or types + a single container (i.e. non nested) overhauling ssz-generic now, implemented tests for bitvector, bitlist, booleans, and uints. Containers still a bit unclear, but looks like it can be done reasonably with a few pre-defined container types.
